📅 08 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1230 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

As COP31 Antalya kicks off, can world move beyond massive promises?

📅 08 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1230 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • With its pulsing music, flashy images and barrage of special effects, the key message in Antalya's marketing video is clear: Turkey, the host of the 31st edition of the UN climate talks, is cool, stylish, modern — and eco-conscious.
  • Both President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and his wife, Emine, make an appearance, with Turkey's first lady calling climate change "one of the most visible manifestations of the burden human activity has placed on our planet.".
  • Industry observers note that from November 9-20, delegates from nearly every country in the world are coming together in the Mediterranean city of Antalya to chart a way out of the climate crisis.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With its pulsing music, flashy images and barrage of special effects, the key message in Antalya's marketing video is clear: Turkey, the host of the 31st edition of the UN climate talks, is cool, stylish, modern — and eco-conscious.

Both President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and his wife, Emine, make an appearance, with Turkey's first lady calling climate change "one of the most visible manifestations of the burden human activity has placed on our planet.".

Industry observers note that from November 9-20, delegates from nearly every country in the world are coming together in the Mediterranean city of Antalya to chart a way out of the climate crisis. Turkey is the official host, and Australia will lead the negotiations. But the problems they'll confront during those 12 days are far more serious than the showy marketing campaign make them out to be.

Severe drought, extreme heat, wildfires and record-low water levels in Europe's main waterways — summer across the continent was dominated by climate emergencies.

And in late August, a series of flash floods triggered by a rock-ice avalanche in Nepal and Tibet washed away entire villages, killing more than 1,400 people and leaving thousands missing. Climate experts have linked the disaster to melting ice and a warming climate.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Globally, carbon emissions are still rising: the UN has concluded that it is no longer possible to keep global temperature rise to 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 Fahrenheit) above pre-industrial levels, the goal agreed at COP21 in 2015.

It has been revealed that the global transition away from polluting fossil fuels like coal, oil and gas will be at the center of attention in Antalya — once again. To date, there's been no consensus on whether and how to transition rapidly away from this main source of global warming.

Despite the setbacks, the world has made some progress thanks to the 2015 Paris Agreement.

David Victor, a climate expert at the University of California San Diego, pointed out that before then, the planet was hurtling toward an average temperature rise of between 3-3.5 C.

Recent findings suggest that if current climate commitments are fully implemented, the latest UN projections show a rise of up to 2.6 C. It's a significant step forward, even though warming of that magnitude will still have worldwide consequences.

"There's no question that we could be doing more," said Victor, though he cautioned against pinning too much on this year's summit.

All agreements at COP need to be unanimous, meaning individual states can quash any sweeping resolutions. Added to that challenge are the ongoing wars, trade conflicts and other economic problems swirling around this year's negotiations.

In a recent development, "It's like a giant Christmas tree in which everybody's hung their different ornaments, and the tree is groaning and more ornaments are being put on it," mentioned Victor. "We have to look at it for what it is: It's a place where people talk about stuff.".

Instead of waiting for all COP member states to agree, Victor sees a better chance for change in what he called "clubs" — smaller alliances of governments and companies working together to advance actual solutions, whether it be in aviation, shipping or electromobility.

Recent findings suggest that "The Paris process is vital. It has to go forward," he told DW. "But all the work is going to be done in clubs.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

An example of this approach was last April's first ever International Conference on Transitioning Away from Fossil Fuels in Santa Marta, Colombia.

Colombia and the Netherlands invited representatives from 57 countries and key sectors to discuss ways to move the world away from coal, oil and gas, after an agreement on a similar plan failed at the 2025 climate summit due to opposition from several oil-producing states.

Recent findings suggest that with an eye to the ongoing trade conflicts and energy crisis, hosts Turkey and Australia have included green industrialization and the clean energy transition among their aims. One goal is to increase the share of electricity in global energy consumption to 35% by 2035, up from around 20% today.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

A recent analysis by the International Energy Agency found accelerating electrification could cut fuel-importing countries' energy bills by more than $400 billion (€357 billion) by 2035, compared to 2025 levels. The idea could appeal to regions dependent on fossil fuel imports — among them Germany and the European Union.

Ahead of COP31, German Environment Minister Carsten Schneider said Germany and the EU wanted to spark new momentum in the "global phaseout of fossil fuels.".

It's wouldn't just be good for the climate, but a chance for many countries to boost their economies and reduce dependence on energy imports, added Schneider in a statement.

Recent findings suggest that oil-producing states like Saudi Arabia, however, aren't interested in deals that will undermine their business model. At recent UN climate conferences, they've repeatedly blocked any final agreements, including phaseout plans.

Even China, despite its massive expansion of wind and solar energy over the last 20 years, could be against the idea. The economic superpower traditionally rejects any outside demands, proposals or interference concerning its national decisions on energy policy.

Every country in the world is affected by climate change, with loss and damage calculated in the hundreds of billions from heat, drought and storms. Worst hit are vulnerable countries in the Global South and island nations, who are at risk of disappearing as sea levels rise.

That's where money comes into play, with developing countries calling for more support to protect their citizens from the harms of global warming. At the 2024 UN climate talks in Baku, Azerbaijan, industrialized nations agreed to free up at least $300 billion annually in climate financing by 2035.

Recent findings suggest that but where exactly all those funds will come from remains hotly debated. At the same time, several major developed countries — most notably, the US — have cut their development aid.

The German government only paid out €4.7 billion from its 2025 budget for international climate financing, down from €6.1 billion in 2024.

"The level of financial support for developing countries today is far from what's needed," said Jan Kowalzig, a climate expert at Oxfam Germany.

Breaking financial promises like this comes at the expense of losing the trust of developing countries and, as a result, the diplomatic power which Germany and other industrialized nations rely on to shape policy to fight climate change.

Cosima Cassel, who focuses on climate diplomacy at the independent think tank E3G in Berlin, believes Turkey's push to turbocharge electrification during an oil crisis could be successful.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

For Cassel, a successful outcome at what are expected to be difficult negotiations in Antalya would reveal actual political will behind the grand agreements.

When it comes to electrification, that means taking the expansion of electricity grids and battery storage capacity seriously — not to mention removing the barriers to further electrification.

This article was originally written in German.

He has a very different way of looking at football, which I like because he tries to constantly attack and be better than the opponent. His teams constantly press, and it’s unusual to see that in Italian football. He’s remained true to his way of understanding football. His team has a recognizable identity and very different characteristics from the others. They’re very physical, but at the same time they have quality players. If, as a coach, you have the ability to convince your quality players to do the defensive work, it means you’re a top-notch coach. It’s wonderful to have coaches like him, and, I repeat, I’m an admirer of Gasperini.”.

Elite players with a terrible penalty record as Lamine Yamal misses another one

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (845 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Planetfootball

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Lamine Yamal missed another penalty at the weekend, meaning he has missed more than he has scored this season, but he is not the only elite player with a pretty poor record.
  • Yamal failed to convert from the spot when Barcelona were trailing 2-0 to Villarreal and even if his blushes were spared thanks to his teammates, it still added to his mixed bag of a penalty record.
  • Yamal has scored 11 and missed three, giving him a success rate of 79% and here are 10 other elite players who are not so great from the penalty spot.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Lamine Yamal missed another penalty at the weekend, meaning he has missed more than he has scored this season, but he is not the only elite player with a pretty poor record.

Yamal failed to convert from the spot when Barcelona were trailing 2-0 to Villarreal and even if his blushes were spared thanks to his teammates, it still added to his mixed bag of a penalty record.

Yamal has scored 11 and missed three, giving him a success rate of 79% and here are 10 other elite players who are not so great from the penalty spot.

Industry observers note that messi used to be absolutely awful at penalties. He missed four in the 2014-15 season and did so again in both of the following campaigns. No wonder he tried passing the ball rather than shooting.

In a recent development, typical of Messi, he clearly identified it as a weakness and worked to improve it. He missed just one a season for the following two campaigns and is now one of the best penalty takers.

His earlier career form does though mean he still makes this list.

Griezmann would choose to have missed 100 penalties if he scored that one in Milan.

The former Atletico man missed a penalty during the Champions League final against city rivals Madrid in the San Siro, a match his team would go on to lose.

Griezmann did at least score in the penalty shootout but could have given Atletico a great chance at victory in the 90 minutes.

That was one of 14 penalties missed in his career to date.

For a player who seemed able to do pretty much whatever he wanted with the ball, Mahrez was oddly poor when it came to penalties.

He’s missed 12 in total, including four for both Leicester and Manchester City.

If you are looking for a player to have missed a penalty for a lot of different clubs, then Edin Dzeko is your man.

He’s missed spot kicks for five clubs and another for his international team, Bosnia and Herzegovina.

He only ever took one for City and missed it before Sergio Aguero resumed duties and his stint at Fenerbahce saves him from a frankly embarrassing record.

He managed to score seven for the Turkish club, missing two, which rescues him somewhat.

Ribery took eight penalties in the 2007-08 season alone but managed to miss two of them.

After that, he was never really given a first-choice run at spot kicks and only took three more for Bayern.

He did have a 100% record for France, though.

The Pro Evo 6 cheat code may have been able to blast them at will from 30 yards but it was not so easy from 12.

He missed a third of the ones he took, of which the majority came whilst he was at Inter.

Had his career ended there, then his penalty record would have been awful but he did redeem himself somewhat with nine scored and one missed for Flamengo in his latter career.

Missing more penalties than you have scored definitely means you are worth including on this list.

Sterling has failed to score six of the 10 penalties he has scored, so no wonder he was taken off penalty duty.

He scored his first-ever penalty back in the 2017-18 season but then missed the next two he took.

Sterling left City with a record of three scored and four missed but was somehow even worse for Chelsea and Arsenal. He took one for each London club and missed both of them.

A 232-goal striker should make for a prolific penalty taker, right? Wrong.

Inzaghi was surprisingly bad from spot kicks, even if he was only given a limited opportunity to take them.

The former Juventus and Milan player only took 25 in his long career and perhaps that is because he missed eight of them.

Most of his misses came from Milan where he scuffed three and managed to score two. No wonder then he took his final penalty nine years before the end of his career.

At one point in his career, Isak was awful at penalties.

When he left Spain for Newcastle in 2022, he had scored six but missed four and since coming to England he has improved a lot.

He missed one in the 2023-24 Premier League season and another in a UEFA Nations League match for Sweden but has scored 13 in the same time period.

His earlier work does mean he has a bad record, for now.

Vinicius Junior took over Cristiano Ronaldo’s number seven shirt but clearly did not inherit his penalty-taking ability.

Of the 20 he has taken, Vinicius has missed six. His most recent came in the 2025/26 Champions League and since then, Kylian Mbappe has been Madrid’s first-choice penalty taker.

Ronaldo, by comparison, has a conversion record of 83%.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Roma fans invaded the Tardini, with the away match having opened only a few days earlier.

At the stadium, everything went smoothly, with the Roman supporters enjoying a team capable of scoring five goals against Parma, thus overtaking Inter in the standings.

Before kick-off, around 2:00 PM, however, an unpleasant incident occurred, which is now circled in red. “We saw these black vans near Arezzo, the maroon banners: we slaughtered them, destroyed them.”.

One of the voice messages sent through the most internal chats among the Roma fans, reported by Repubblica.

The Giallorossi and Torino supporters clashed along the Autostrada del Sole, near the Arno Est service area.

The National Observatory for Sporting Events is now waiting for the investigators from the DIGOS (Italian Special Operations Unit) of Turin, Parma, Florence, and Rome to complete the reconstruction of the facts before taking any necessary disciplinary action.

Recent findings suggest that roma and Turin fans could face another suspension of away matches. This scenario cannot be ruled out, given what happened on the highway. Recalling Saturday’s events, approximately 140 Roma ultras attacked 70 members of the “Torino Hooligan” group, but when traffic police arrived on the scene, no one was left.

Sources indicate that now investigators from the Rome Digos, along with other Italian police stations, are trying to identify the individuals involved. One initial finding is already certain: all those involved in the clashes avoided entering the Tardini or Maradona stadiums. The final report will determine the Observatory’s decisions. For Roma and Turin fans, there is a real risk of another suspension of away matches.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After finishing their training at Trigoria, Roma arrived in Paris on the eve of the highly anticipated match against Luis Enrique’s PSG.

Gian Piero Gasperini presented the match at a press conference, addressing problems related to his possible options and more.

The Giallorossi coach commented on the matchup against a giant of modern football: “It’s the first time we’ve faced PSG. We’ll have to understand their parameters, hopefully reducing their effectiveness.”.

Regarding the early comebacks in the competition, the coach said: “The Champions League is the most key competition in the world. You can put in great performances, but there are also incidents, and the best players around.”.

Gasp recalled the match against Atalanta: “The match against Atalanta was tough. We were down to 10 men, but this is a different game. Roma is approaching this competition after years, and for us it’s a measure of what we’re doing.”.

Then the general from Grugliasco discussed the solutions he will adopt to limit his opponents: “Clearly, in these types of matches, more solutions are needed; we don’t have any previous parameters. Beyond tactics, personality will be important, as will the ability to counter their play.”.

The Parisians will have several injuries, but that won’t be a problem for them: “There’s no scientific answer to injuries. There’s been a great improvement in diagnoses, and PSG still has a squad that allows them to make up for absences. As I remarked before, PSG is a team that knows how to compensate for the absences of very strong players with organization and with substitutes, who are absolutely valuable.”.

Recent findings suggest that the matches against Real Madrid and Manchester United can teach us something. “This is the Champions League, a competition of incidents. You have to be excellent in every situation, there are some great players and sometimes it’s not even enough to put in strong performances, even though I think that’s the best way to get results. You have to be careful about mistakes because they often pay the price.”.

#94571. Latest Update: 8 naff football-related presents you could get this Christmas: Soap, Cards, Monopoly…

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1061 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Planetfootball ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: 8 naff football-related presents you could get this Christmas: Soap, Cards, Monopoly…

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1061 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Planetfootball

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It’s getting close to that time of year when your relatives know you like football and so try their best to get a gift, but they don’t always quite get it right.
  • Liking football means you often get just about anything as a gift provided it has your club’s badge on it (if you’re lucky) and let’s all hope that none of us open any of these under the tree this year.
  • Here are eight wonderfully awful football-related Christmas gifts for this year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s getting close to that time of year when your relatives know you like football and so try their best to get a gift, but they don’t always quite get it right.

Liking football means you often get just about anything as a gift provided it has your club’s badge on it (if you’re lucky) and let’s all hope that none of us open any of these under the tree this year.

Here are eight wonderfully awful football-related Christmas gifts for this year.

When we heard Bristol City were selling grass we thought that’s one way to raise the transfer budget but turns out it is of the turf variety.

The Robins are releasing soap that has been “scientifically” made to replicate the smell of the pitch at Ashton Gate so you can shower with the smell of a pitch that is 18th in the Championship right now.

We will give them credit for the excellent slogan of “because you’re turf it” but it has naturally opened them to such jokes as it smelling like the s**t football that gets played on it.

Profits will at least go to the club’s foundation.

Introducing the Ashton Gate-scented soap to raise funds for the Robins Foundation’s work in communities across Bristol.

According to recent reports, available online and in-store. https://t.co/kbDyZ1XbTC.

— Bristol City FC (@BristolCity) November 24, 2026.

This is worth it for the pun alone.

Ipswich are selling a Christmas candle called Ipswicks which they describe as a Luxury Scented Christmas Candle smelling of Pine, Eucalyptus & Cedarwood.

We don’t know what the Ipswich marketing department thinks of their fans though as there is a warning to not touch the tin as it may get hot.

Club-branded playing cards is not that unusual but we are including these because Arsenal have decided to charge their fans £70 for three packs of cards.

For that money, you get a commemorative box that has the names of the players that won the title last season and the cards are in the colours of the kits used last campaign but we hope no one buys that because that is an incredible waste of money.

Just imagine, you’ve had your Christmas dinner and someone suggests some card games and then pulls those out. Awful.

If you think £70 is too much, then don’t worry, you can get a single pack of cards for £18.

In a recent development, honestly, there are so many things from the United store that could have made the list. Firstly, they are selling quite literally a cardboard box for £10. They also have a sack so the jokes write themselves.

But the one item we have picked out is the United-branded Monopoly board they are selling for £50.

Recent findings suggest that realising that there are not 28 United-related places to go on a Monopoly board, the club decided to name each square after moments in their history, fair enough. What isn’t fair enough is that the final square, which is the most expensive slot on the board, comes with the title of “2016/17 WON THE LOT.”.

Sorry? We’ve checked the league table and can’t help but see you were sixth? And surely the FA have made a mistake because they seem to think that Arsenal won the cup that year? While we are at it, you will want to have a word with UEFA because they seem to think that Real Madrid won the Champions League that season.

Sources indicate that “The lot” United are referring to is actually the League Cup, Europa League and Community Shield. Did Jose Mourinho commission this?

Well they’ve got to pay their massive wages somehow.

Man Utd truly shocking in 2026-27 Premier League wage bill vs. position comparison.

It may have slipped your attention but did you know that League Two side Northampton Town are now owned by a Brazilian consortium fronted by Alexandre Pato?

The Cobblers are doing their best to spread the word by releasing a number of Brazil-inspired pieces of merchandise and so we are picking the half and half scarf that has Northampton in the middle and the Brazil flag on the ends.

It feels like the kind of thing that will end up in the National Football Museum in 100 years’ time.

The problem with football is that it is fast-moving and so one product that is good one year can rapidly become out of date. Step forward Arne Slot figure.

Liverpool commissioned a set of Soccerstarz of the 2025/26 squad but, unfortunately for Slot, is still hanging around in a storage cupboard somewhere.

They are trying their best to shift it, reducing it down to £1 or 90p if you are a club member, but even he looks annoyed at still being there.

Do you even love your club if you don’t wear socks promoting the club’s owners?

Any Leicester fans afraid of being called a plastic ought to buy themselves a pair of these fetching purple socks that do not display really anything to do with the club but instead the brand of King Power.

There is a Leicester badge but it is on the sole of the foot meaning no one will see it but at least you show off your favourite Bangkok-based travel retail conglomerate.

Recent findings suggest that bonus points to the Foxes for the Sonic the Hedgehog scarf. We don’t know why either.

In a recent development, it’s late on Christmas Day. You’re full to the brim but excited for the day’s football tomorrow.

You fancy a little tipple to round off the festivities and so what better way to scratch that itch and get prepared for tomorrow than with a Sheffield United shot glass with a picture of a chip butty on the side of it?

For just £3.50, or you can pay in four interest-free payments of 87p, you can have a shot glass which is “a nod to the no-fuss, unpretentious spirit that runs through every corner of S2 [where Bramall Lane is].

Apparently it “carries the kind of quiet pride that doesn’t need to shout” but it just makes us feel rather queasy.

'Never Again!': Holocaust remembrance under pressure

📅 08 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1277 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that young people pose inside a crematorium oven at the Buchenwald concentration camp memorial, laughing while they give the Nazi salute and take pictures of each other.
  • It has been revealed that "Incidents like this have become more frequent in recent years.
  • It has been revealed that wagner is part of the curatorial team behind the exhibition "Never Again!
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that young people pose inside a crematorium oven at the Buchenwald concentration camp memorial, laughing while they give the Nazi salute and take pictures of each other. "In a sense, they're trophies to post on social media for them to boast about — breaking the ultimate taboo," Jens-Christian Wagner, director of the Buchenwald and Mittelbau-Dora Memorials Foundation, told DW.

It has been revealed that "Incidents like this have become more frequent in recent years. We have seen memorial trees planted in honor of concentration camp victims cut down. When something like this happens — and it happens regularly — I find it particularly despicable because, because it ultimately kills these people a second time," added Wagner.

It has been revealed that wagner is part of the curatorial team behind the exhibition "Never Again! Against Forgetting the Crimes of the Nazi Regime" in Bonn's Bundeskunsthalle, or the Art and Exhibition Hall of the Federal Republic of Germany. Wagner said Holocaust remembrance is under pressure, and the subject of intensifying attacks.

Critics have dismissed remembrance as a "cult of guilt" or "national masochism." With right-wing populism on the rise and historical revisionism becoming more common, Wagner worries about how Germany will remember the victims murdered by the Nazi regime. He is also concerned about the future of democracy. And soon, there will be no Holocaust survivors left to tell the true story of what happened.

This latest exhibition tackles this concern head-on with numerous works of art and historical artifacts.

"I hope that perhaps even some people who don't already believe it's key to confront Nazi crimes will find their way to the exhibition," Wagner said. Memorial sites also attract visitors who aren't necessarily convinced of the need to confront these parts of history. Many of them are students.

"Let's not kid ourselves: When a teacher indicates 'We're going there,' it's always a mandatory visit," he noted.

It has been revealed that for today's young people, the Nazi era seems like the distant past, Wagner explained. "When you tell them to remember something that their grandparents didn't even experience, it naturally feels like an emotional burden. They can practically see the finger being wagged at them, and that doesn't exactly encourage learning.".

It has been revealed that A two-hour lecture won't have much of an impact if pupils aren't even paying attention. Instead, Buchenwald organizes full-day programs that allow students to explore historical sources together and make sense of history for themselves.

The next step, Wagner remarked, is to show young people that this chapter of history isn't closed. Visitors are encouraged to make connections between the past and current events like migration, for example.

"For the longest time, people have been discussing migration almost exclusively in terms of threats to public safety and crime. This broadly marginalizes certain groups — a mechanism that also worked for National Socialism," he remarked.

Eva Umlauf, 83, knows firsthand what it means to experience exclusion in its most extreme form. She is a patron of the Bonn exhibition.

In November 1944, Umlauf was just 2 years old when she, her pregnant mother and her father were deported by the Nazis from the Novaky labor camp in Slovakia to Auschwitz-Birkenau, the notorious Nazi concentration and extermination camp. She was saved from the gas chambers by mere days; the Nazis stopped using the chambers as the Red Army advanced, hoping to hide evidence of their crimes.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The camp was liberated on January 27, 1945. Three months later, Umlauf's sister Nora was born. But her father, her mother's siblings and her grandparents were all murdered. Eva barely survived herself. She suffered from tuberculosis, rickets and whooping cough, as well as edema caused by starvation. "Forget about the child. She won't survive," a doctor told her mother. But he was wrong.

Her mother returned to what was then Czechoslovakia with her two daughters, settling in Trencin. Eva Umlauf has no conscious memories of Auschwitz, but she carries her family's trauma deep within her.

Recent findings suggest that her mother never talked about what happened. Even so, Eva knew from an early age that she was a survivor. Her family rarely mentioned the camp by name, but one sentence came up again and again: "They stayed there." Eva knew that meant "they" were dead. And then, there was the number tattooed onto her arm: A26959.

Recent findings suggest that her mother taught her daughters not to draw attention to their Jewish identity — antisemitism was widespread throughout Czechoslovakia at the time. The small family managed to avoid harassment.

Eva Umlauf wanted to become a pediatrician, so she studied medicine. In the 1960s, she met her future husband, Jakob, who had also survived the Holocaust. He was an architect, active in Munich's Jewish community. They married in 1966, and she moved to Germany. She could hardly have imagined that she would one day live in the country of the perpetrators. "I don't hate Germans," she said. "But I cannot forgive. How can you forgive the deaths of 6 million people?".

It wasn't until much later that she first spoke publicly about the horrors of her early childhood. In 2011, she delivered a commemorative speech in Auschwitz on the anniversary of the camp's liberation. Since 2025, she has served as chair of the International Auschwitz Committee. A heart attack in 2014 motivated her to write her first book. "I was in intensive care. I thought to myself: If I get out of here healthy, I'll write a book.".

Her memoir, "The Number on Your Forearm is Blue Like Your Eyes," was first released in 2016. The English translation followed in 2024. Since its publication, hardly a day has passed without someone asking Eva Umlauf to share her story.

She is appalled by the disrespectful behavior of young people at former concentration camps and by growing ignorance about the Holocaust. Sometimes, people even ask if she's too old to have a tattoo. But she also recalls a young man on the Munich subway who noticed the number on her arm and told her: "I want to apologize to you for what my ancestors did to you.".

Umlauf never imagined that antisemitism would once again become so widespread in Europe and the United States. Nor did she expect the rise of Germany's far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party.

Sources indicate that "I go into schools. I'm so overwhelmed by the number of requests asking for my availability. And yet, the AfD is growing faster than I can reach students. It makes me think all this work is for nothing," she told DW.

Sources indicate that germany must never again fall under a right-wing dictatorship, she stressed. "'Never again' sounds nice, but all I can say is: It's happening again! Wouldn't 'Here We Go Again: Never Again' make a good title for the exhibition?".

She also shared her message to young people in the exhibition catalog, "Never Again": "You are not responsible for the crimes of your grandparents and great-grandparents. But you are responsible for the future. […] You are the generation that will shape our world. Make it a place where everyone can grow up safely, regardless of their background, faith or skin color.".

She continues: "You don't have to be perfect. You just have to stay alert. Take care of your country.".

Recent findings suggest that the exhibition "Never Again! Against Forgetting the Crimes of the Nazi Regime" in the Bundeskunsthalle in Bonn runs through May 2, 2027.

This article was originally written in German.

#94567. A tribute to Dean Ashton, the best striker England never had

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1100 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Planetfootball ↗ Open Full Page

A tribute to Dean Ashton, the best striker England never had

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1100 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Planetfootball

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, after shining for Norwich City and West Ham, Dean Ashton became one of England’s big hopes, but a combination of factors meant we never saw the best of the striker for the Three Lions.
  • Every time an England squad is confirmed for a major tournament, we get the inevitable complaints about certain players missing the cut, albeit for different reasons.
  • Occasionally we’ll see complaints that the squad gets packed with established names at the expense of exciting youngsters, while at other times we’ll wind up with younger players from top clubs making the cut ahead of in-form talents from less-fancied clubs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, after shining for Norwich City and West Ham, Dean Ashton became one of England’s big hopes, but a combination of factors meant we never saw the best of the striker for the Three Lions. It’s a sad ‘what if’ story.

Every time an England squad is confirmed for a major tournament, we get the inevitable complaints about certain players missing the cut, albeit for different reasons.

Occasionally we’ll see complaints that the squad gets packed with established names at the expense of exciting youngsters, while at other times we’ll wind up with younger players from top clubs making the cut ahead of in-form talents from less-fancied clubs.

The latter was certainly the complaint of many when Theo Walcott made the squad for the 2006 World Cup ahead of Darren Bent coming off the back of an impressive season with Charlton.

But there was another player who could feel hard done by: Dean Ashton.

Sources indicate that being overlooked was a recurring theme. In fact, you have to wonder how many more of those predicted future England XIs – which brought notoriety to the likes of Dean Parrett and Patrick Roberts – he’d have featured in had he come through the ranks of a top club’s academy rather than Crewe’s, which was still known for producing top talents but certainly not at the same rate as in the 90s.

However, those who saw him in the early part of his career can attest he was always a special talent.

Indeed, after he left the Cheshire club for Norwich in January 2005 with them in the top half of the Championship, they proceeded to go 18 games without a win and only stayed up on the final day of the season.

Even then, aged just 21, he looked as close as you could get to the complete striker, scoring 20 in 27 games for the Alex and adding seven for a struggling Canaries side after making his top-flight bow.

That tally included a quite lovely volley against Manchester City, the finish of a young man who felt he couldn’t fail with anything he attempted.

Looking at Ashton, most would never have identified him as a man capable of such subtlety, but a lot of that can be put down to England’s specific record with players of his ilk.

The Three Lions have often resisted demanding too much of their frontmen: either giving them the ‘Substantial man up top’ responsibilities or ensuring they’re nippy with tidy finishing ability – as if anticipating every single pairing should be modelled on the platonic ideal of Niall Quinn and Kevin Phillips.

In fact, going all-in on a combo that was happy with some nice moments and a seventh-place finish does seem quite England, on reflection.

Anyway, by tempering expectations, the sight of a more complete frontman has tended to confuse people, leading to Ashton – even off the back of another great season in 2005-06, overlooked for that summer’s World Cup in Germany.

Indeed, when Walcott was handed a surprise call-up having played no first-team football since January that season, Darren Bent – not Ashton – was the man who many said should feel hard-done-by.

But while not as prolific as some in that half-season, Ashton was capable of scoring goals you wouldn’t back others to produce – not least his clincher in the FA Cup quarter-final win over Manchester City.

The sight of a hefty striker dancing through a defence with grace and tidy footwork is an underrated genre of goal, like a bear performing ballet, and this was on par with Johan Elmander doing the same for Bolton a few years later.

It highlighted Ashton had that touch of class needed to unlock bunched defences, and – with fitness question marks around some of the other squad members that summer – it’s very easy to make retrospective demands for his inclusion with the benefit of a decade’s distance.

Of course, Ashton’s fitness in the summer of 2006 would almost prove ironic given the struggles later in his career, beginning with his first England call-up not long after that World Cup.

An injury in training, following a challenge from Shaun Wright-Phillips, ended up being one from which he never fully recovered, though there was one more hot season – and one stand-out goal – to celebrate before his early retirement in 2009 at the age of just 26.

Ashton’s consolation goal in West Ham’s May 2008 defeat to Manchester United was to overhead kicks what Ashton himself was to No.9s: very different to what we’ve come to expect from the genre, but that doesn’t mean it doesn’t work.

Overhead kicks, generally speaking, can be divided into the Rivaldo-style self-assisted efforts and the side-on excellence produced by the likes of Eidur Gudjohnsen for Chelsea against Leeds United.

Ashton’s was neither of these things, yet the ugly beauty of the finish was a sight to behold.

It has been revealed that ashton eyes up the ball like a sniper keeping sight of a moving target, but the process is complicated by his own continued need to readjust. And yet, with the close attentions of Rio Ferdinand and the looming sight of Edwin van der Sar, not once did he seem to consider the prospect of not making a clean contact on the ball.

Would it have been easier to go for a header? Yes. Would it have been more efficient to bring the ball down and beat Van der Sar that way? Almost certainly. Would we be talking about the goal if he’d done either of those things? Heavens no.

Industry observers note that sadly for Ashton, whose one England cap would come that summer, that was pretty much the end of it. He managed just a handful of games the following season before his ankle flared up once more and he made the difficult decision to walk away from the game.

Had England qualified for that summer’s European Championships, he might have been given his chance at a major tournament.

But then again, a healthy Dean Ashton might itself have been enough for England to qualify in the first place.

Sources indicate that with England misfiring on more than one occasion in tournaments, conversations invariably turn towards those who played and failed to score. But perhaps we should be talking about the missing piece of the jigsaw who wasn’t there.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A statue of Albert Einstein holding a scientific manuscript sits outside the US National Academy of Sciences building in Washington DC.Credit: Paul J.
  • According to recent reports, patch: After a delay, the report discussed in this story was released by the US National Academies of Sciences, Engineering and Medicine on 24 November.
  • Science publishers take too long to retract or correct research papers, a report by the US National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine (NASEM) finds.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A statue of Albert Einstein holding a scientific manuscript sits outside the US National Academy of Sciences building in Washington DC.Credit: Paul J. Richards/AFP via Getty.

According to recent reports, patch: After a delay, the report discussed in this story was released by the US National Academies of Sciences, Engineering and Medicine on 24 November. The academies remarked that the problem was with erroneous references added to the report in response to peer review.

Science publishers take too long to retract or correct research papers, a report by the US National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine (NASEM) finds. Standards for fixing errors are also inconsistently applied across journals, it says.

Why retractions data could be a powerful tool for cleaning up science.

Why retractions data could be a powerful tool for cleaning up science.

There are no data on how long a retraction or correction presently takes, because journals do not generally disclose when they were alerted to underlying problems; the NASEM report states that they should start doing this. On average, according to the Retraction Watch database, retractions occur around 2.4 years after a paper is published. The report recommends that, in most cases, editorial review processes be completed within 12 weeks, and should rarely stretch beyond 6 months — at least when editors are looking at concerns over a single paper.

It has been revealed that “The big picture is, the process is too slow,” says Randy Schekman, a cell biologist at the University of California, Berkeley, who chaired the 13-person committee that produced the NASEM report. A prompter and more transparent process would strengthen the reliability of the scientific record, he says.

The report was due to be published online on 19 November but was delayed after journalists at Science noted that it contained some references with fabricated first names for authors, a possible sign that large language models had been used to write or edit the material and that it had been insufficiently checked.

“It’s unfortunate that there were these flawed references in a report about fixing the literature,” says Jennifer Byrne, a cancer researcher and research-integrity sleuth at the University of Sydney in Australia, who first flagged the concern to Science when reviewing the report, which was shared ahead of publication with media outlets.

Sources indicate that the report had two main aims: to speed up the process of retraction or correction and to lower the “tremendous emotional barriers” for authors to correct honest mistakes in the record, Schekman says. “Part of the problem is that it’s too rare for a paper to be retracted,” he adds.

Retractions of old papers are on the rise: when should bad science be culled?

Retractions of old papers are on the rise: when should bad science be culled?

According to recent reports, it also suggests that journals shouldn’t wait for complaints to reach them, but instead “take proactive steps” to identify errors and integrity problems. These might include journal-wide audits, or regularly monitoring social-media feeds and online platforms where post-publication issues are raised, it claims.

Existing guidelines for publishers, such as those from the Committee on Publication Ethics (COPE) in London, urge only a “timely” response to concerns1, without setting out expected schedules, and don’t suggest that journals scan online platforms for complaints.

According to recent reports, “A major theme running through the report is that we have to distinguish between retraction or correction, and research misconduct,” notes Dorothy Bishop, a research-integrity sleuth in Oxford, UK, who was on the NASEM committee. Authors shouldn’t associate a retraction with the stigma of research misconduct, she indicates. And although journal editors sometimes wait for a university to investigate whether there is misconduct before correcting a paper, they shouldn’t, she adds.

More than 10,000 research papers were retracted in 2023 — a upcoming record.

More than 10,000 research papers were retracted in 2023 — a new record.

Calls for changing these attitudes aren’t fresh: journals have long emphasized that retractions can result from honest mistakes. In a 2022 editorial, Holden Thorp, the editor in chief of Science, urged that the processes of issuing corrections or retractions and making a determination of misconduct should be kept separate2, and COPE guidelines already emphasize the point. But “there are still plenty of people who see a correction or retraction as an allegation of fraud”, says Thorp, who was also on the NASEM committee. “Hopefully, this report will accelerate the recognition of the distinction,” he says.

Industry observers note that simply put, you have six attempts to guess a word. There will be a clue for each one to focus your mind a little.

Type in your first guess then hit enter. Each tile will change colour to indicate if the letter is in the correct position, elsewhere in the word or does not appear at all. A green tile means the letter is in the correct position; an orange tile means the letter is elsewhere in the word; a grey tile means that letter is not in the word at all.

If you are struggling, you will see a hint button that becomes available from your fourth attempt. Clicking it will reveal a tile, though note this is only available to logged-in consumers.

In a recent development, you can also click Give Up if you’re really struggling and just want to be put out of your misery. It’s not one for the purists, but it’s nice to have the option!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Kylian Mbappe has reached 75 Champions League goals, putting him alongside Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo in one of the competition’s most exclusive clubs.

Robert Lewandowski and Karim Benzema are the only two others in the history of the European Cup to have reached that number of goals in the competition.

The Real Madrid superstar is already chasing down the two greatest goalscorers in Champions League history – but could he one day overtake them in the all-time charts?

According to recent reports, he’s on the right track. He hasn’t quite done reached the milestone in as emphatic style as Messi, who still holds the record for getting there at the youngest age and in the fewest games, but he has a considerable headstart on his idol, and the Champions League’s all-time top scorer, Ronaldo.

Mbappe scored his 75th and 76th goals in Madrid’s statement 5-1 comeback victory over PSV, adding another landmark to an already remarkable European career – albeit one that still lacks him getting his hands on the Champions League trophy.

The Frenchman has needed 103 appearances to reach 75 Champions League goals, putting him somewhere between Messi and Ronaldo for speed.

According to recent reports, messi needed eight games fewer to reach the milestone of 75 Champions League goals. Ronaldo, meanwhile, needed eight games more, having scored his 75th Champions League goal against Schalke in March 2015.

Mbappe also reached the landmark at a considerably younger age than Ronaldo, although Messi was still the youngest of the three, having done so about six months younger than the Los Blancos Galactico.

It has been revealed that however, Mbappe has already surpassed both players for assists at the same stage, registering 30 compared to Ronaldo’s 24 and Messi’s 20. Considering that the two era-defining icons are also the all-time top assist-providers in Champions League history, the 27-year-old France international finds himself on the right trajectory to one day smash that record too.

His overall rate of goal contributions is almost identical to Messi’s, although the Barcelona legend was more prolific when it came to goals per minute.

Why Nvidia CEO's affair with alleged Chinese spy matters for AI race

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang's admission to an affair with a woman whom US intelligence officials believe was working as a spy for China could have profound implications for the $5 trillion (€4.47 trillion) tech giant.
  • The Financial Times first reported on Huang's affair with Alice H., an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based customer of Nvidia, which has been suspected of trying to circumvent export controls to get advanced Nvidia chips into China.
  • The newspaper reported that the US government and its intelligence community believe she was recruited as a spy by China's Ministry of State Security intelligence agency.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang's admission to an affair with a woman whom US intelligence officials believe was working as a spy for China could have profound implications for the $5 trillion (€4.47 trillion) tech giant.

The Financial Times first reported on Huang's affair with Alice H., an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based customer of Nvidia, which has been suspected of trying to circumvent export controls to get advanced Nvidia chips into China.

The newspaper reported that the US government and its intelligence community believe she was recruited as a spy by China's Ministry of State Security intelligence agency.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

US government officials drafted a memo about the allegations shortly before US President Donald Trump traveled to Beijing for a summit with Xi Jinping in May.

Huang's relationship with the alleged Chinese spy has exposed him and the company to criticism that it may have allowed China to obtain valuable trade secrets as Beijing tries to gain an edge in the race to develop advanced AI models.

In a recent development, nvidia is initiating an investigation led by independent board members and an external law firm. It stated in a statement that Huang "has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.".

"The board prioritizes US national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of Nvidia and its shareholders," the organization said Sunday. "While the board has no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, the board's inquiry will examine all available information.".

The manufacturer's shares fell in early trading on Monday.

While US intelligence officials have not commented publicly on the claims, Trump — with whom Jensen Huang has a close relationship — has backed the Nvidia boss.

"He's an honorable guy," said Trump. "I have not spoken to him ​about it. I just know he's a ​fine person, but you never know what is going on. I hope everything's fine.".

Tim Culpan, an Asia tech reporter who has covered Nvidia and Huang closely for years, told DW that while Nvidia's fundamental strengths as a company remain in place, Huang is hugely personally damaged by the story.

"They're still going to make great chips and they're going to sell them to millions of customers around the world who want the best AI chips in the world," he said.

"His opinion is going to carry a lot less weight now. And that, in the long term, will flow through to Nvidia and Nvidia's own corporate interests. So it won't be immediate. It's really a fact that he doesn't have the sway or the power that he might have had one week ago simply through this.".

Richard Windsor, a tech analyst and the founder of research tech giant Radio Free Mobile, mentioned the news could be very serious for Nvidia given how much the company has revolved around Huang for decades.

"This problem is particularly acute because Jensen Huang is very hands-on, meaning that the key decisions that led to its success were ultimately taken by him and because there is no obvious successor," he said.

"I suspect we are about to find out just how much the market thinks that the firm is dependent on its iconic founder and CEO.".

Nvidia and Huang's attitude toward China and potential Chinese customers has been a bone of contention with US intelligence officials — despite Huang's close relationship with Trump.

It has been revealed that huang has repeatedly lobbied Trump to ease restrictions on the sale of Nvidia chips to China. A 2025 export control deal heavily curbed sales, but Trump subsequently permitted the export of older H200 Nvidia chips to China in return for the US government receiving a cut of the sales.

Industry observers note that however, that deal has been complicated and bogged down by Washington's strict export-license review. China has also initiated import controls, despite strong demand from Chinese companies. China lacks access to the most advanced AI-capable chips. Beijing wants to develop its own alternatives but has struggled to catch up.

Huang has argued that Chinese dependence on Nvidia's chips would prevent rivals such as Huawei from catching up and boosting China's ambitions to dominate AI supply chains.

Sources indicate that however, that argument has been dismissed by many US intelligence officials. They fear that unlimited Chinese access to the most advanced Nvidia chips would boost China's domestic AI sector, lead to its AI models catching up with the leading US models and see the chips being used in Chinese military applications.

The US-China rivalry has become a central theme in the global AI story, with both countries seeking to gain an upper hand in the technology. Leading US AI executives such as Anthropic's Dario Amodei have argued that US AI companies can't afford to take a prolonged pause to allow safety standards in AI to catch up, if they're going to prevent Chinese firms from gaining an advantage.

Washington's central fear over Huang's affair is that it could have led to Beijing obtaining vital trade secrets or other key information about how Nvidia makes its most advanced chips.

In a recent development, windsor thinks Huang will survive the "severe test" due to his importance to the company. He also cast doubt on the extent to which Beijing and its leading tech firms have learned from Nvidia's chips, pointing to China's own chip ambitions and commitment to have its firms buy its own semiconductors.

"I am far from convinced that Chinese AI has materially benefited from technology or illicit chip imports that it gained from Nvidia," he noted.

The news comes at a particularly challenging moment for Nvidia, which has benefited massively from the AI boom thanks to its position as the leading maker of cutting-edge semiconductors needed for AI applications.

Nvidia's valuation has soared dramatically in recent years as companies rushed to buy its chips, becoming the world's first $5 trillion company in October 2025.

However, doubts over the sustainability of the $9 trillion capital expenditure AI boom have sparked a major sell-off in stocks related to the boom in recent weeks. The Democrats' sweeping victories in the US midterms have added to the doubts, given the strength of voter opposition to data center construction in the US.

Industry News: Most expensive goal in Liverpool history gives Iraola era lift-off

⏱️ ~19 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A quick sprint, a well-placed pass and an instinctive finish.
  • Sources indicate that anfield has witnessed plenty of significant goals down the years but never had this crowd seen one that cost £248m to make.
  • Liverpool are a work in progress under Andoni Iraola but with each minute of each game you can see signs of things knitting together, and if Barcola and Isak are finding harmony, with Florian Wirtz in behind, then, perhaps, this journey will start to accelerate.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A quick sprint, a well-placed pass and an instinctive finish. Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak will have done this dozens of times in training but here, on a squally Sunday afternoon, this combination secured a little piece of history.

Sources indicate that anfield has witnessed plenty of significant goals down the years but never had this crowd seen one that cost £248m to make. Liverpool invested a near quarter-billion pounds on Barcola and Isak for bigger occasions than a tussle with Brighton and Hove Albion, but this rapid interchange felt like a significant moment.

Liverpool are a work in progress under Andoni Iraola but with each minute of each game you can see signs of things knitting together, and if Barcola and Isak are finding harmony, with Florian Wirtz in behind, then, perhaps, this journey will start to accelerate.

This was an important afternoon for Liverpool’s head coach, a difficult assignment against high-flying, well-respected opponents in Brighton, who arrived on Merseyside having won their last four Premier League fixtures with a combined aggregate of 15-0, including a 3-0 thumping of reigning champions Arsenal.

But Liverpool rose impressively to the challenge and there are grounds for saying this was the most significant success to date for Iraola, whose team defended relentlessly to preserve a clean sheet. They are up to fourth now after this 2-0 success and deserve their position.

“I’m very happy,” Iraola remarked. “We faced a very good opponent, similar to Villarreal [in the Champions League]. It’s difficult to defend them a lot of times and it was key how we started. We needed to be aggressive, recover balls, win our duels, be dangerous in transitions: I think we’ve done it.”.

According to recent reports, and how. Iraola was able to march towards the Kop at the end, to clap the supporters and acknowledge only Liverpool’s fifth (and his first) Premier League win at Anfield in 2026, and it was evident he had a spring in his step from what he had seen.

Whether the game would have flowed in the direction it did had Brighton taken the lead can only be speculated but what a glorious chance they wasted for us to find out: in the 13th minute, five swift, one-touch passes bamboozled Liverpool’s defence and created space for Yasin Ayari.

In a recent development, with the goal at his mercy, Ayari could have made things exceptionally uncomfortable but he leant back and blazed over. He clasped his face and grimaced, knowing what had gone begging in front of the Kop; four minutes later, his misery was exacerbated.

"He's GOT to hit the target!" Yasin Ayari missed a golden chance to put Brighton ahead against Liverpool 🫣 https://t.co/Qz7G3sXCpP.

Liverpool’s lead was secured with an element of good fortune but, equally, the tenacity of Ronald Araújo and Wirtz was instrumental in pressing Brighton back to the point that they were panicking; Wirtz’s shot, deflected off Pascal Gross past Bart Verbruggen, compounded it all.

“I think everyone in the stadium – and you as well – felt there was a missed opportunity for us,” groaned Fabian Hürzeler, the visitors’ head coach. “It’s not only after the goal or the goals they scored. Before they scored, we had two big chances. I think it was just the difference that they scored and we didn’t score.”.

It would be wrong to say Wirtz was doing cartwheels – perhaps he knew immediately he would not get the goal – but it was an important moment for him and you could feel the sense of goodwill towards him from team-mates and supporters alike.

Florian Wirtz's deflected shot has put Liverpool ahead minutes after Brighton had a great chance of their own ⚽️ https://t.co/b6mRvl2rSR.

Remarkably, this was the first time Liverpool had scored in the first half at Anfield in a Premier League fixture since May 9 and, with that momentum, it led to one of those periods when they started attacking in waves and carried the crowd with them.

What they needed was a second goal to arrive quite quickly and that is what happened when Barcola won possession, scuttled forward and played a perfectly weighted bobbling ball into Isak’s path; the Swede did the rest, calmly finishing from eight yards.

Recent findings suggest that everything with Isak feels to be going under the radar at the moment, but that is six goals in six Premier League appearances. He is starting to show the consistency and killer instinct that everyone felt he would. Iraola will be hoping it continues for the foreseeable future.

Alexander Isak scores to double Liverpool's lead at Anfield! 💥 https://t.co/oYs2jnHZEb.

“The performance was really good,” remarked Isak, the quiet assassin. “We were really solid against a really good team. The first half is what we really want to be about. It was about intensity, winning balls and countering.”.

Brighton, as much as Hürzeler protested, could not properly recover, though this is no criticism. They remain committed to attack, they struck the frame of the goal when Ayari tried to punish an Alisson Becker mistake and the desire to keep pushing ensured Liverpool could never relax.

What Liverpool had going for them this time, however, was an intensity to preserve a clean sheet and nobody embodied the indefatigability more than Araújo, the Uruguay international whose loan from Barcelona is looking an increasingly shrewd piece of business.

Two moments stood out: one thunderous tackle on substitute Malick Yalcouyé in front of the Main Stand that had the locals roaring their approval, another in the first half when he was on the floor but still managed to head away to thwart Maxim De Cuyper.

Sources indicate that they remember those moments as much as the stardust that Barcola and Isak provide. Put it all together and it might just be a launchpad for Iraola.

"The performance was really solid" Alexander Isak reacts after scoring in Liverpool's win against Brighton 🗣️ https://t.co/Zei2tmWVix.

Sources indicate that iraola has his first Premier League home win in charge of Liverpool thanks to a 2-0 victory over Brighton. The hosts netted twice in the first half through Wirtz’s deflected strike off Gross and Isak’s close-range finish. This result moves Liverpool above Chelsea and up to fourth, just a point behind third-place Brighton, who suffer their first defeat in any competition since August 30.

Three points at Anfield 😍 #LIVBHA https://t.co/AnAlNgOzlu.

In a recent development, still, Brighton can’t find a way through Liverpool’s resilient defence. Araujo’s well-time sliding challenge on Kostoulas draws huge cheers from the home fans.

It has been revealed that ronald Araujo has become a cult figure very quickly and he’s just provided the moment of the second half with a challenge that was a well received by those in the Main Stand as a goal. Liverpool are working relentlessly to preserve their clean sheet and Andoni Iraola is imploring his players to retain their focus until the end.

According to recent reports, there will be four minutes of added time. Brighton need a goal as soon as possible. Liverpool are closing in on an impressive win.

So wasteful from Brighton... They have a great chance to put the ball into the box with a free kick, but De Cuyper wastefully rolls out it out of play. With Gross also stood over it, you expected him take it. Liverpool then make a late change as Tsimikas replaces Kerkez for the final few minutes.

It has been revealed that gakpo drives forward and smashes a wild long-range shot wide. His end-product has been lacking today, but he’s undoubtedly caused Brighton problems with his dribbling, movement and directness.

A spell of Brighton pressure ends as Rutter can’t quite find Kostoulas with a low cross. The young striker stays down and replays show that Jacquet stood on his foot as the defender attempted a clearance. However, it’s quickly checked and cleared by VAR. There wasn’t much in the challenge at all.

Kerkez scampers into Brighton’s box, reaching the byline, but he can’t dig out a cross as the chance disappears. Brighton will need to throw everything forward soon.

Now, that double change from Liverpool is here. Barcola and Isak depart to large applause, with Ngumoha and Koumas cheered on as they run onto the pitch.

As expected, Rutter is on. He replaces Ayari, who will think back to his missed chance and shot off the post in the first half.

Gakpo brilliantly turns Costinha, who pulls the winger back to deservedly pick up a booking. Both sides look to be readying changes, with Ngumoha, Koumas and Rutter poised to enter the action.

Brighton seem to have hit a wall in this second half. They’ve struggled to create chances since the break. Liverpool are working really hard defensively.

Industry observers note that once again, Liverpool break through Gakpo. This time, it comes from a Brighton corner, but Gakpo’s cross for Isak at the back post is read by Dunk.

It has been revealed that in his first involvement since entering the action, Nyoni ends a slick Brighton move by taking the ball off De Cuyper’s toe in the penalty area with a much-needed clearance. He seems to be limping after he was caught by De Cuyper.

Wirtz’s game is over and he departs to be replaced by Nyoni in Liverpool’s first change.

After some treatment for Wirtz, Vuskovic eventually takes the free kick. It’s in such an inviting position, but the defender gets too power on his strike and whips it over the bar.

This game is still very much in the balance, even though Liverpool have a two goal advantage, and it speaks volumes about both teams’ commitment to attack. The questions the respective head coaches are asking of their players are relentless but the players are responding by being adventurous in how they attack and where they want to get on the ball. How Andoni Iraola and Fabian Hurzeler deploy their substitutes will be significant.

Liverpool are holding firm, with Brighton yet to create an opportunity in this second half. Ayari is apprehended by Wirtz to win a free kick on the edge of the area. Despite committing the foul, Wirtz has stayed down and is clutching his ankle.

Brighton make another change and it’s a straight swap in midfield as Yalcouye replaces Chema Andres, who hobbles off the pitch.

With Brighton requiring at least two goals to avoid defeat, they’ll need to push a lot of men forward, which will open up space for Liverpool to exploit on the break. If there is one, the next goal in this game is crucial.

Sources indicate that liverpool break through Gakpo, who sprints from inside his own half into the penalty. He tries to release Isak, but his pass is intercepted by Vuskovic as he’s swarmed by the Brighton defence. Gakpo waited too long and should have played the pass earlier.

Sources indicate that kerkez isn’t switched on and fails to deal with a long ball, allowing Gomez to race in behind. Van Dijk covers Kerkez and blocks Gomez’s pass, with Kostoulas sprinting up in support.

We are back under way for the second half. Hurzeler has made one half-time alteration, with Hinshelwood replacing Boscagli, who was booked just before the break. Meanwhile, Liverpool are unchanged as they look to protect their two-goal advantage.

Industry observers note that wirtz’s wickedly deflected strike off Gross and Isak’s neat finish from close range mean Liverpool are two goals in front against Brighton. The visitors have also looked dangerous going forward, with Ayari wasting a golden chance when the score was still goalless, before hitting the post in the 36th minute. As it stands, this result would move Liverpool into fourth and a point behind Brighton, who need a massive second-half performance.

Two goals to the good for @LFC 😮‍💨 A Pascal Gross own goal puts the Reds ahead, before Alexander Isak fires in the second 🔴 https://t.co/AglQOyUIoY.

Brighton are desperate to find a goal before the break as Kostoulas’ fierce shot is batted away by Alisson, whose goal is living a charmed life. Boscagli then receives a yellow card for blocking Barcola’s off-the-ball run.

No getting away from the fact that Brighton simply haven’t got started and it’s a huge surprise. What chances they have had came from Liverpool’s own shortcomings and it is impossible to think they will be so off the pace in the second period. Fabian Hurzeler has remained composed, which is more than can be said for Oliver Boscagli, who looks like he is playing pass the parcel, so anxious is he to get rid of the ball - often with a mistake.

Recent findings suggest that on the counter, Gomez tries to find Ayari with a pass, but Jacquet’s touch knocks the ball out of Liverpool’s box. There will be three minutes of added time to end this half.

Araujo forces a save as he sprints forward from his right-back position to receive a clipped pass from Mac Allister, before shooting from a tight angle to sting the palms of Verbruggen with a drilled effort.

Gakpo drives at Brighton’s defence and then nearly squeezes a low cross to the supporting Isak, but Dunk’s crucial intervention with his outstretched leg prevents a chance.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

David Moyes is hopeful he will have a fully-fit squad to choose from as Everton look to extend their impressive form away to Brentford on Monday night (8pm GMT).

After the recent international break, the Blues resume their Premier League campaign in west London aiming to cement their place in the top six of the table.

Ahead of his pre-match press conference at Finch Farm on Friday, Moyes was presented with a signed frame by his former Blues midfielder Leon Osman and current captain James Tarkowski to mark his record-breaking 593rd match in charge of Everton against Brentford on Monday.

And the Toffees boss was confident he will have all options available for his starting XI in the capital.

'Hopefully everybody will be fit and available on Monday night for the Brentford game," said Moyes. "We've not had anyone return from international duty with any problems. We've got another few days to go before game day so hopefully we won't pick up any.".

Despite having a small squad to work with this season, Moyes also spoke about his desire to be flexible with his team selection when possible.

He added: "I want us to be flexible where we can alter things if we have to.

In a recent development, "I think the form of Harrison [Armstrong] and Jimmy [Garner] and Kiernan [Dewsbury-Hall] has made it easy to select [the midfield]. It's not always just the form.

Recent findings suggest that "We want to choose the right games and not overplay them. But it is quite difficult when you don't have quite so many players.".

Brentford will be without main striker Igor Thiago for the visit of the Toffees, the Brazil international serving the first game of a three-match suspension following his red card for violent conduct in the 2-0 loss to Brighton & Hove Albion before the recent international break. In his absence, veteran Callum Wilson is in line to lead the Bees' attack.

Meanwhile, centre-back Nathan Collins is a doubt after sustaining a knee injury during the Republic of Ireland’s 1-0 defeat by Austria last Saturday. The 25-year-old returned to Brentford for further assessment and missed the Republic of Ireland’s 3-0 victory over Kosovo on Tuesday.

Full-back Aaron Hickey is another concern after picking up a hamstring problem while playing for Scotland against Switzerland.

Assistants: Nick Hopton and Adrian Holmes.
